reader.requirement: In random or dynamic access the DELETE removes the record whose prime record key equals the prime key data item's content (whatever was read last, and whatever alternate keys hold); no such record is the invalid key condition, status 23, with nothing removed.
reader.edition-search: grep of IndexedConnector.cs (Edition hits only at READ PREVIOUS and READ duplicate-status rows), KeyedIoEmitter.cs (only registration) and SequentialIoEmitter.cs (registration, SELECT WHEN): none on the DELETE key path; the access-mode switch is Access == KeyedAccess.Sequential
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf30_04 covers random and dynamic deletes by prime key with junk elsewhere in the area and absent keys; a dynamic DELETE of a key other than the one just read via READ NEXT, LOW-VALUES key and alternate-index removal are not exercised

probes.printed: DEL K01 00 / ALT A01 00 K02A01 (K01 gone from the duplicate alternate) / LOW IK 23
probes.expected: record of prime key K01 removed under every key; a LOW-VALUES key names no record: invalid key 23

probes.printed: DEL 999 AFTER READ NEXT OF 001 00 / DEL000 IK 23 / LEFT 001AAA, 002BBB, END
probes.expected: dynamic: the key item (999) names the record, not the one READ NEXT returned (001); absent key 000 gives INVALID KEY with 23

reader.notes: The emitter passes the whole record area and the runtime slices the prime key from it (AreaKey), removes the record's entries in every key tree in one statement, and answers 23 when the prime tree has no frame.

refuter.evidence: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-093/dyn1.cob (dyn1-002), dynamic access with an alternate key: READ NEXT returns 001, key item set to 002, DELETE 00 removes 002 (not the record read); DELETE with the area as left by READ NEXT of 003 removes 003. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.3.4 GR3.
